$comment: Real documents slimdoc is tested against, which are NOT committed — they are
other people's files. `test/fixtures/local/` is gitignored; this manifest is not,
so the coverage stays documented on a clone that has none of them.
Tests that need one of these skip with a notice when it is absent. To populate:
copy a document matching the description to test/fixtures/local/<file>. Anything
with the right shape works — the sha256 below is the copy these expectations were
measured against, and a mismatch is reported as a notice, not a failure.
Why this tier exists: every fixture in test/fixtures/corpus/ is hand-written XML
and hand-written PDF byte streams, so it encodes the same assumptions as the
extractor. Wherever the extractor guessed, those fixtures agreed with it. Each
entry below broke something the 347-test suite passed straight through.

fixtures.name: deck-textboxes
fixtures.description: A deck built almost entirely from plain text boxes rather than placeholders — 3 slides, ~95 non-empty paragraphs, none carrying bullet properties of its own.
fixtures.proves: Bullet inheritance must not over-apply. These paragraphs are non-placeholder shapes, so they resolve through the master's otherStyle, which carries no bullet — even though the same master's bodyStyle carries buChar. A naive 'inherit from the master' fix bullets all 95 lines.

fixtures.name: deck-mixed
fixtures.description: 12 slides, 4 charts with axis titles, 2 tables, 12 images, and paragraphs of all three bullet kinds: 14 explicit, 11 inheriting, 200 explicitly buNone.
fixtures.proves: Chart axis titles are visible slide text and must survive the default (they do not today). Bullet resolution must produce all three outcomes from one deck.

fixtures.name: deck-hidden
fixtures.description: 10 slides, one genuinely marked show="0" by PowerPoint.
fixtures.proves: Slide numbering must be stable across --hidden: --pages 6 and '## Slide 6' have to mean the same slide either way, and the same slide PowerPoint numbers 6.

fixtures.name: paper-2col
fixtures.description: A two-column academic paper with a running title, numbered pages and body text set ragged-right.
fixtures.proves: Genuine two-column reading order must keep working — this is the regression guard for the two-column-table fix, which narrows the same code path.

fixtures.name: paper-figures
fixtures.description: An academic paper whose pages carry diagrams built from scattered positioned labels.
fixtures.proves: Grid preservation must not fence prose or figure labels. Eight pages produce 35 fenced blocks today, and because fenced content is exempt from cleaning, unwrap never runs on them.

fixtures.name: form-rotated
fixtures.description: A multi-page form whose pages carry /Rotate 90.
fixtures.proves: Page height must come from the unrotated box. pdf.js rotates the viewport but not getTextContent() coordinates, so on a rotated page the margin bands land on the wrong axis and body text is deleted as running furniture.
